targets.title: Keeping one's distance: The influence of spatial distance cues on affect and evaluation.
targets.evidence_quote: The first replication attempt focused on Study 4 of Williams and Bargh (2008), in which the “spatial priming manipulation” was reported to have influenced people's feelings of emotional attachment to familiar people and places.
targets.outcome_quote: The present work attempted two fairly exact replications of studies reported by Williams and Bargh (2008). Neither study supported the original results.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The overall verdict explicitly covers both attempted replications, of the social-closeness and food-calorie effects.

reasoning: Two new undergraduate samples directly retest Studies 4 and 3 from one published paper. Other cited priming findings and the calculation of a perceptual-priming effect size motivate the work rather than constitute additional replication targets.
